AUR build process egress to temp.sh or github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo AICommand & Control High
Hunts the campaign's C2/staging endpoints (temp.sh paste/file-share and the attacker-controlled github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo repo) when the connecting process is an AUR build tool, npm/node, or a shell child of one. Combines process-cmdline mentions (for HTTPS path strings) with network-event hostname matches. Rationale: Pivots on the two article-specific C2/staging endpoints (temp.sh, github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo from Phase 8 of the kill-chain reconstruction) tied to a build-context parent process. The dual pivot (process-cmdline OR DNS/URL) catches both direct git clones of the attacker repo (where the URL lives in argv) and downstream HTTPS uploads (where only DNS/SNI sees temp.sh).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1567.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DFIR team manually cloning github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo for malware analysis (filter on responder hostnames)
  • Developer using temp.sh as a legitimate scratch file-share service from a normal shell (parent will not be makepkg/yay/paru)
  • Reverse-engineering CI job pulling the malicious repo into a sandbox for static analysis
  • Threat-intel ingestion pipeline that mirrors known-bad domains to update IOC feeds
  • Cached resolution of temp.sh from a non-build process that survives in DNS cache and gets attributed to the wrong parent
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("malware-analyst","ir-responder","detlab") and DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "detlab"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent-process chain (look up InitiatingProcessParentFileName / ParentBaseFileName); pull pacman.log to map the connection back to the AUR package that triggered it. 2) Contain: block temp.sh and the fardewoak repo at the egress proxy; isolate the host; rotate every credential touched on that host (SSH/GitHub/npm/cloud) per the article's IR guidance — these are the assets the stealer harvests. 3) Hunt: correlate this DeviceId with UC1 (atomic-lockfile install) and UC3 (credential file fan-out) to confirm the full kill-chain; expand the search 6h either side of the connection across all Arch hosts to spot other infected machines.
let buildParents = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","npm","node","bash","sh","fakeroot"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (buildParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (buildParents)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak","nodejs-argo")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="ProcessCmdline",
            Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            ChildBin = FileName,
            Detail = ProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (buildParents)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak","nodejs-argo")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="NetworkEvent",
            Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            ChildBin = "",
            Detail = strcat(RemoteUrl, " (", tostring(RemoteIP), ":", tostring(RemotePort), ")")
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let buildParents = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","npm","node","bash","sh","fakeroot"]);
union
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any (buildParents)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak","nodejs-argo")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source="ProcessCmdline",
            Detail = ActingProcessCommandLine
),
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("temp.sh")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername=SrcUsername, Source="DnsActivity",
            Detail = DnsQuery
),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak/nodejs-argo")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername=SrcUsername, Source="WebSession",
            Detail = strcat(Url, " UA=", HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AUR Build Process Egress to Atomic Arch C2 (temp.sh / fardewoak)
id: 9c4f6a2b-7d8e-4f1c-a3b9-2e5d7c8f1a4d
description: Detects DNS or HTTP egress to temp.sh or github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo initiated by an AUR helper, makepkg, npm/node, or a shell child of one — the staging / exfil channels of the Atomic Arch campaign.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/400-aur-packages-hijacked-atomic-arch-campaign
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/14
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.exfiltration
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'temp.sh'
      - 'fardewoak'
      - 'nodejs-argo'
    Image|endswith:
      - '/makepkg'
      - '/pacman'
      - '/yay'
      - '/paru'
      - '/npm'
      - '/node'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/git'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) (@process.command_line:(*temp.sh* OR *fardewoak* OR *nodejs-argo*) OR @dns.question.name:(temp.sh OR *.temp.sh)) @process.name:(makepkg OR pacman OR yay OR paru OR trizen OR pikaur OR aura OR npm OR node OR curl OR wget OR git OR bash OR sh)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^temp\.sh$/i ContextImageFileName=/\/(makepkg|pacman|yay|paru|trizen|pikaur|aura|npm|node|curl|wget|git|bash|sh)$/i)
| OR
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(makepkg|pacman|yay|paru|trizen|pikaur|aura|npm|node|bash|sh)$/i CommandLine=/(temp\.sh|fardewoak|nodejs-argo)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, DomainName, CommandLine], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
(| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","npm","node","bash","sh") AND (Processes.process="*temp.sh*" OR Processes.process="*fardewoak*" OR Processes.process="*nodejs-argo*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="temp.sh" OR DNS.query="*.temp.sh") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | search process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","npm","node","curl","wget","git")]
(| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","npm","node","bash","sh") AND (Processes.process="*temp.sh*" OR Processes.process="*fardewoak*" OR Processes.process="*nodejs-argo*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="temp.sh" OR DNS.query="*.temp.sh") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | search process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","npm","node","curl","wget","git")]
Non-browser process fan-out reading SSH/npm/Docker/AWS/browser credential stores on Arch host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Rust-based credential stealer's signature behaviour: a single short-lived process reading four or more high-value credential files (~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.aws/credentials, Chrome/Firefox cookie DBs, Slack/Discord session stores) within a short window, while excluding the legitimate browsers/CLIs that normally touch those paths. Rationale: Targets the credential-targets list directly enumerated in the article body (SSH keys, GitHub/npm/Docker/cloud tokens, browser cookies, Slack/Discord/Teams sessions). The article's stealer is Rust-compiled with an opaque process name, so the high-signal pivot is the FAN-OUT (>=4 distinct credential stores in 2 min) by a single unknown binary — that's the smoking gun a normal browser/CLI never produces.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup tools (restic, borg, duplicity) snapshotting the user's home directory — touch many credential files in quick succession
  • Dotfiles sync utilities (chezmoi, yadm) on first-run reading every config
  • Configuration management agents (ansible-pull, chef-client, puppet) re-reading host facts/agent creds
  • Endpoint AV/EDR full-disk scans reading every file — exclude by signed AV process name
  • Migration helpers like `gh auth setup-git` or `gcloud auth login` re-reading multiple credential stores in one workflow
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/lib/backup" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("restic","borg","duplicity","chezmoi","yadm","ansible","puppet-agent","chef-client","falcon-sensor","mdatp")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName + SHA256 — if SHA256 is unseen elsewhere in the org and the binary lives under /tmp, /dev/shm, ~/.cache or an AUR build dir, treat as confirmed. Capture the binary for static analysis. 2) Contain: kill the process tree, isolate the host, force-rotate EVERY credential the binary read (the article's IR guidance: SSH keys, GitHub/npm/cloud tokens, browser sessions, Slack/Discord/Teams). Invalidate AAD sessions for the user. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId → UC2 (was anything exfiltrated to temp.sh?) and UC4 (was eBPF persistence installed?); pivot SHA256 across the org; review pacman.log for the AUR package that introduced it.
let CredPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/glab-cli","Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data","/.config/Slack/storage","/.config/discord","/.config/Teams","/.kube/config","/.vault-token"]);
let KnownGood = dynamic(["ssh","scp","sftp","git","ssh-agent","gpg","gpg-agent","firefox","chrome","google-chrome","chromium","brave-browser","slack","discord","teams","code","gh","glab","aws","docker","npm","kubectl","vault","gnome-keyring-daemon","keepassxc","keyring","snap"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpen","FileRead","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName in~ ("Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data",".vault-token")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownGood)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(FolderPath),
            Targets = make_set(FolderPath, 25),
            First = min(Timestamp), Last = max(Timestamp),
            Reads = count()
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, bin(Timestamp, 2m)
| where DistinctTargets >= 4
| order by Last desc
let CredPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.aws/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data","/.config/Slack/storage","/.config/discord","/.kube/config","/.vault-token"]);
let KnownGood = dynamic(["ssh","scp","sftp","git","gpg","firefox","chrome","chromium","slack","discord","code","gh","aws","docker","npm","kubectl","vault"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths) or TargetFileName in~ ("Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data",".vault-token")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (KnownGood)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Targets = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 2m)
| where DistinctTargets >= 4
| order by Last desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR EXECVE) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_* OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.aws/credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR *cookies.sqlite OR *Cookies OR *key4.db OR *Login\ Data OR */.kube/config OR */.vault-token)) -@process.name:(ssh OR scp OR sftp OR git OR firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR slack OR discord OR code OR gh OR aws OR docker OR npm OR kubectl OR vault OR gpg OR gpg-agent OR gnome-keyring-daemon OR keepassxc)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/(id_|known_hosts)|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|cookies\.sqlite|Cookies$|key4\.db|Login Data|\/\.config\/(Slack|discord|Teams)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.vault-token)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(ssh|scp|sftp|git|gpg|firefox|chrome|chromium|slack|discord|teams|code|gh|aws|docker|npm|kubectl|vault|gnome-keyring-daemon|keepassxc)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function={ count_distinct=count(TargetFileName, distinct=true) | first_seen=min(_time) | last_seen=max(_time) })
| count_distinct >= 4
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as files dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_files min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*cookies.sqlite*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*key4.db*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Login Data*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/storage*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord*") AND Filesystem.process_name!="ssh" AND Filesystem.process_name!="scp" AND Filesystem.process_name!="sftp" AND Filesystem.process_name!="git" AND Filesystem.process_name!="firefox" AND Filesystem.process_name!="chrome" AND Filesystem.process_name!="chromium" AND Filesystem.process_name!="slack" AND Filesystem.process_name!="discord" AND Filesystem.process_name!="gh" AND Filesystem.process_name!="aws" AND Filesystem.process_name!="npm" AND Filesystem.process_name!="docker" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path _time span=2m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_files >= 4 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
eBPF program load or pinned object created from non-system parent on Arch host AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the article's rootkit-style persistence primitive: an eBPF program loaded or a BPF object pinned under /sys/fs/bpf/ by a process that isn't one of the legitimate eBPF consumers (Cilium, Tetragon, Falco, systemd-networkd, BCC tools). Particularly noisy when paired with a recent makepkg/pacman/yay parent within the last hour. Rationale: Targets the article's explicit persistence claim — 'eBPF-based persistence to hide processes and file activity' (Phase 5 of the kill-chain). The clean signal is BPF objects pinned by a process that isn't a known eBPF runtime; the leftouter join to recent makepkg/pacman/yay activity raises confidence when the load happens inside an AUR build window.
ATT&CKT1014 T1547 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin running ad-hoc `bcc-tools` like execsnoop, opensnoop, biotop for performance diagnostics
  • Kubernetes CNI upgrade installing a new Cilium/Calico version that hasn't refreshed its process-name list
  • Custom in-house observability agent loading eBPF probes (allowlist by SHA256)
  • Cloud-init or Ansible role provisioning Tetragon/Falco for the first time on a fresh host
  • kernel-debug session via `perf record` writing perf-event maps under /sys/fs/bpf/
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate the BPF object — `bpftool prog show` and `bpftool map show` on the host (read-only); capture InitiatingProcessSHA256 and the BPF object name. If the loading process isn't a known runtime and lives under /tmp / /dev/shm / an AUR build path, treat as confirmed rootkit. 2) Contain: do NOT rely on host-resident tools (they may be hidden by the rootkit) — pull the host out of the network, image the disk from a clean rescue environment, and rebuild from trusted media per the article's IR guidance. 3) Hunt: pivot the loader SHA256 across the org; check every Arch / WSL2-Arch host for `/sys/fs/bpf/` content from non-system processes in the last 30 days; correlate with UC1 (atomic-lockfile install) on the same host.
let KnownEbpfConsumers = dynamic(["systemd","systemd-networkd","systemd-resolved","bpftool","cilium-agent","cilium","tetragon","falco","tracee","sysdig","containerd","runc","crun","docker","dockerd","kubelet","calico-node","snap","mdatp","falcon-sensor","perf","bpftrace"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownEbpfConsumers)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru")
    | project AurTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, AurFile=FileName, AurCmd=ProcessCommandLine
  ) on DeviceId
| extend BuildContextNearby = iif(isnotempty(AurTime) and Timestamp between (AurTime .. AurTime + 1h), true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          BpfObject = FolderPath,
          BpfFile = FileName,
          Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatorParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          BuildContextNearby, AurFile, AurCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let KnownEbpfConsumers = dynamic(["systemd","systemd-networkd","bpftool","cilium-agent","tetragon","falco","tracee","sysdig","containerd","runc","crun","dockerd","kubelet","calico-node","mdatp","falcon-sensor","perf","bpftrace"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (KnownEbpfConsumers)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          BpfObject = TargetFilePath,
          Initiator = ActingProcessName,
          InitiatorCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious eBPF Object Pinned Outside Known eBPF Consumers (Atomic Arch Rootkit)
id: 2a7c9e5d-4f3b-4c1e-8d6a-9b3c5e7f1a2c
description: Detects creation or modification of eBPF objects under /sys/fs/bpf/ by a process that is not one of the standard eBPF runtime consumers (Cilium, Tetragon, Falco, systemd, BCC). Aligned with the Atomic Arch campaign's described 'eBPF-based persistence to hide processes and file activity' when the malware gains root.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/400-aur-packages-hijacked-atomic-arch-campaign
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/14
tags:
  - attack.t1014
  - attack.t1547
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|startswith: '/sys/fs/bpf/'
  filter_known:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/systemd'
      - '/systemd-networkd'
      - '/bpftool'
      - '/cilium-agent'
      - '/tetragon'
      - '/falco'
      - '/tracee'
      - '/sysdig'
      - '/containerd'
      - '/runc'
      - '/dockerd'
      - '/kubelet'
      - '/bpftrace'
  condition: selection and not filter_known
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @file.path:/sys/fs/bpf/* -@process.name:(systemd OR systemd-networkd OR bpftool OR cilium-agent OR tetragon OR falco OR tracee OR sysdig OR containerd OR runc OR dockerd OR kubelet OR bpftrace OR mdatp OR falcon-sensor)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/^\/sys\/fs\/bpf\//
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(systemd|systemd-networkd|bpftool|cilium-agent|tetragon|falco|tracee|sysdig|containerd|runc|dockerd|kubelet|bpftrace|mdatp|falcon-sensor|perf)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as image values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/*" AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified") AND Filesystem.process_name!="systemd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="systemd-networkd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="bpftool" AND Filesystem.process_name!="cilium-agent" AND Filesystem.process_name!="tetragon" AND Filesystem.process_name!="falco" AND Filesystem.process_name!="tracee" AND Filesystem.process_name!="containerd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="runc" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as image values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/sys/fs/bpf/*" AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified") AND Filesystem.process_name!="systemd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="systemd-networkd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="bpftool" AND Filesystem.process_name!="cilium-agent" AND Filesystem.process_name!="tetragon" AND Filesystem.process_name!="falco" AND Filesystem.process_name!="tracee" AND Filesystem.process_name!="containerd" AND Filesystem.process_name!="runc" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Persistence written to user shell init or systemd user units from AUR build/install scriptlet AIInstallation Medium
Hunts post-install persistence dropped by hijacked AUR packages — writes to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.config/systemd/user/, ~/.config/autostart/, /etc/cron.d/, or /etc/profile.d/ when the writer's parent (or grandparent) is makepkg/pacman/yay/paru/trizen/pikaur/aura. Legitimate Arch packages rarely modify the invoking user's home directory. Rationale: Combines two article-grounded signals: the persistence file locations a build-time payload would naturally use (cron/systemd/shell-rc/profile.d/ld.so.preload) AND a writer that is an AUR helper or shell carrying a PKGBUILD/.install context. Legitimate AUR packages install to /usr/... — a write to ~/.bashrc or /etc/cron.d from makepkg's child is the differentiator.
ATT&CKT1546.004 T1053.003 T1547.013
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Shell-framework AUR packages (oh-my-zsh-git, bash-completion variants) that DO legitimately modify ~/.zshrc/~/.bashrc by design
  • AUR packages shipping legitimate systemd units to ~/.config/systemd/user/ (rare but exists — e.g. user-mode VPN clients)
  • pacman hooks updating /etc/ld.so.cache after a library install (different from ld.so.preload but path may confuse)
  • Dotfiles-management AUR packages (chezmoi, stow) intentionally placing files in home
  • First-time provisioning runs where a fresh user account gets its initial rc files populated by an install script
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "oh-my-zsh" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "bash-completion" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "chezmoi" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "stow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the actual file content written — `cat` the persistence target and look for the malicious payload signatures (calls to /tmp/.* binaries, references to atomic-lockfile/temp.sh/fardewoak, base64-encoded blobs, ProcID hiding logic). Cross-check the source PKGBUILD against AUR upstream via `pacman -Qi` + `git log` on the AUR repo. 2) Contain: revert the persistence file to its pre-install state (or delete the rogue entry), kill any process started from it, isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the AUR package name across the org to find every host that installed it; correlate with UC1/UC2/UC3 on the same DeviceId to confirm full kill-chain; remove and quarantine the package from local AUR caches.
let PersistencePaths = dynamic(["/.bashrc","/.bash_profile","/.zshrc","/.profile","/.bash_aliases","/.zprofile","/.config/systemd/user/","/.config/autostart/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/systemd/system/"]);
let AurTools = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","fakeroot"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (PersistencePaths) or FileName in~ (".bashrc",".zshrc",".profile","ld.so.preload")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (AurTools)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (AurTools)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD",".install","post_install","pre_install","makepkg")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          PersistenceFile = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName),
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

status: experimental

Miasma and Hades Are Spreading Now: Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspicious Files

StepSecurity
2026-06-18 9 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Miasma and Hades worms are spreading across npm and PyPI, running on import and project open. See how Dev Machine Guard's Suspicious Files detects them.

ATT&CKT1027 T1195.002
SHA256dc48b09b2a5954f7… e1342a80d4b5e83d… c539766062555d47… 7069e28a5806db4a… b86c5ae9e95bd841…

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Miasma Phantom Gyp — 100-300 byte binding.gyp written outside a normal native-addon build
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Hades on-import payload — Bun runtime fetched and executed by Python interpreter
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] IDE / AI assistant auto-execute — Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini spawning shell or runtime via project-open hook · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma and Hades Are Spreading Now: Detect Them on Developer Machines with Suspi
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Miasma/Hades 'Suspicious Files' — IDE & AI-assistant auto-execute hooks dropped · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Worm propagation — `npm publish` or `twine upload` from interactive developer endpoint
Miasma/Hades 'Suspicious Files' — IDE & AI-assistant auto-execute hooks dropped AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the exact filenames the article calls out as Miasma/Hades execution triggers — .vscode/tasks.json, .vscode/setup.mjs, .claude/setup.mjs, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json, .github/setup.js, and the 157-byte binding.gyp. These artifacts run when a project is opened in an IDE/AI assistant or when npm install hits a native build, bypassing lifecycle-script scanners. Rationale: Every filename matched (binding.gyp, .vscode/tasks.json, .vscode/setup.mjs, .claude/setup.mjs, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json, .github/setup.js) is named explicitly in the article's Suspicious Files table. The 512-byte ceiling on binding.gyp brackets the article's 157-byte Phantom Gyp value with margin. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native-addon npm packages do ship binding.gyp — most are larger than 512 bytes but some toy modules sit at ~200 bytes
  • Developers hand-authoring a real .vscode/tasks.json for a build task
  • Cursor/Claude Code template repos that legitimately seed .cursor/rules/setup.mdc
  • Internal scaffolding tools (yeoman, plop) that drop .github/setup.js during repo init
  • Dotfile syncers (chezmoi, mackup) copying .claude/settings.json across machines
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","devenv.exe","msiexec.exe","git.exe","chezmoi.exe","yo.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the file's SHA256 and content. binding.gyp under 200 bytes that gyp-binds to a JS file in node-gyp pre-build is the Phantom Gyp pattern; .claude/setup.mjs and .cursor/rules/setup.mdc that contain network/shell calls are the auto-execute payload. Identify what package, GitHub org, or AI assistant session dropped it. 2) Contain: quarantine the file on the endpoint, revoke any npm/PyPI publishing tokens stored on that user's profile (.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, OS keyring), and disable the user's npm/PyPI accounts pending password+2FA reset. 3) Hunt: query DeviceProcessEvents for child shells spawned from the IDE (code.exe, cursor.exe) on this host since the file was written; query NetworkEvents for bun.sh downloads; pivot SHA256 across the fleet to find other affected devs.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" and FileName in~ ("tasks.json","setup.mjs"))
   or (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" and FileName in~ ("setup.mjs","settings.json"))
   or (FolderPath has @"\.cursor\rules\" and FileName =~ "setup.mdc")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.gemini\" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.github\" and FileName =~ "setup.js")
   or (FileName =~ "binding.gyp" and FileSize < 512)
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","devenv.exe","msiexec.exe","git.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\" and TargetFileName in~ ("tasks.json","setup.mjs"))
   or (TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\" and TargetFileName in~ ("setup.mjs","settings.json"))
   or (TargetFilePath has @"\.cursor\rules\" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.mdc")
   or (TargetFilePath has @"\.gemini\" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json")
   or (TargetFilePath has @"\.github\" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.js")
   or (TargetFileName =~ "binding.gyp" and TargetFileSize < 512)
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe","devenv.exe","msiexec.exe","git.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) (@TargetFilename:(*\\.vscode\\tasks.json OR *\\.vscode\\setup.mjs OR *\\.claude\\setup.mjs OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc OR *\\.gemini\\settings.json OR *\\.github\\setup.js) OR @TargetFilename:(*/binding.gyp))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("(?i)(\\\\\\.vscode\\\\(tasks\\.json|setup\\.mjs)|\\\\\\.claude\\\\(setup\\.mjs|settings\\.json)|\\\\\\.cursor\\\\rules\\\\setup\\.mdc|\\\\\\.gemini\\\\settings\\.json|\\\\\\.github\\\\setup\\.js|\\\\binding\\.gyp$)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(code|cursor|devenv|claude|msiexec|git)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

IDE / AI assistant auto-execute — Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini spawning shell or runtime via project-open hook AIExploitation High
Detects VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, or Gemini spawning a shell or scripting runtime where the parent or child command line references one of the Miasma/Hades trigger files. This catches the actual execution side of the auto-execute hooks (.vscode/tasks.json runOn:folderOpen, .claude/setup.mjs SessionStart, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json). Rationale: The article names exact triggers: .vscode/tasks.json (runOn: folderOpen), .claude/setup.mjs (SessionStart hook), .cursor/rules/setup.mdc (loaded on project open), .gemini/settings.json (settings injection). Pairing IDE parent + scripting child + one of those file strings in either cmdline is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/
ATT&CKT1546 T1059.007 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VS Code task that legitimately runs npm test referencing a tasks.json the dev wrote
  • Cursor running a benign linter via setup.mdc on project open
  • Developer using .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen for legitimate dev environment setup (docker compose up)
  • node.exe spawning from VS Code's integrated terminal during normal dev work where the command line happens to contain '.vscode\\' as a project path
  • Claude Code SessionStart hook configured by the user for a legitimate context-loader script
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker compose","npm test","npm run dev","jest","vitest","playwright") and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("fetch(","child_process","base64","atob(")))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the contents of the referenced setup.mjs/setup.mdc/tasks.json. A few lines of shell is normal; obfuscated JS, base64 blobs, child_process.spawn, or fetch() to non-corp domains is malicious. Check git blame on the file — Miasma/Hades commits will be very recent and from an unfamiliar author or via dependency update. 2) Contain: kill the shell/bun/node child, isolate the dev workstation if the payload made network calls, revoke npm/PyPI publish tokens, force password+2FA reset on the dev's npm and PyPI accounts. 3) Hunt: pivot the project path across DeviceFileEvents fleet-wide — any other dev who cloned that repo and opened it in their IDE got the same payload; look for outbound to bun.sh and to the C2 the payload calls.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","devenv.exe","claude.exe","gemini.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","node.exe","python.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","setup.mdc","tasks.json","binding.gyp",".claude\\",".cursor\\",".gemini\\",".vscode\\")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","setup.mdc","tasks.json","binding.gyp")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("code.exe","Code.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","devenv.exe","claude.exe","gemini.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","node.exe","python.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","setup.mdc","tasks.json","binding.gyp",".claude\\",".cursor\\",".gemini\\",".vscode\\")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs","setup.mdc","tasks.json","binding.gyp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\devenv.exe OR *\\claude.exe OR *\\gemini.exe) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\python.exe) @CommandLine:(*setup.mjs* OR *setup.mdc* OR *tasks.json* OR *binding.gyp* OR *\\.claude\\* OR *\\.cursor\\* OR *\\.gemini\\* OR *\\.vscode\\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(code|cursor|devenv|claude|gemini)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|bun|node|python|sh|bash)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(setup\\.mjs|setup\\.mdc|tasks\\.json|binding\\.gyp|\\\\\\.claude\\\\|\\\\\\.cursor\\\\|\\\\\\.gemini\\\\|\\\\\\.vscode\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","code.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","devenv.exe","claude.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","node.exe","python.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mdc*" OR Processes.process="*tasks.json*" OR Processes.process="*binding.gyp*" OR Processes.process="*\\.claude\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\.cursor\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\.gemini\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\.vscode\\*" OR Processes.parent_process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.parent_process="*tasks.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","code.exe","cursor.exe","Cursor.exe","devenv.exe","claude.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","bun.exe","node.exe","python.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mdc*" OR Processes.process="*tasks.json*" OR Processes.process="*binding.gyp*" OR Processes.process="*\\.claude\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\.cursor\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\.gemini\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\.vscode\\*" OR Processes.parent_process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.parent_process="*tasks.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime)
Worm propagation — `npm publish` or `twine upload` from interactive developer endpoint AIActions on Objectives High
Miasma and Hades self-replicate by stealing the developer's publishing token and immediately republishing infected versions of every package that token can publish. Detects npm publish or twine upload originating from a developer endpoint that is NOT a known CI runner. Threshold-style: >=3 distinct package names published from one host within a 10-minute window is the worm fan-out signature. Rationale: Article: 'Once Miasma or Hades lands on a developer machine, it searches for npm and PyPI publishing tokens, then republishes infected versions of every package that token can publish.' Fan-out of >=3 publishes from a non-CI host inside 10 minutes is the exact worm signature — legitimate human publishing of multiple packages in 10 minutes is rare. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineer doing a coordinated monorepo release with lerna/changesets/nx that legitimately publishes 5-20 packages in one shot
  • Maintainer republishing a fixed version across a family of related packages after a hotfix
  • Self-hosted CI runner the parent-process filter doesn't know about (e.g. local act runner)
  • Developer testing publish flow against a private registry (verdaccio) — same npm publish command line
  • First-time npm publish for a new project with a couple of related packages (workspace publish)
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("lerna","changesets","nx release","rush publish","workspace"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the actual package names published in the 10-min window and the registry URL each went to (--registry flag, or default npmjs.org/pypi.org). Cross-check against the dev's known package portfolio — if package names match every package they own, this is the worm. Check for an `.npmrc` token used non-interactively (no terminal). 2) Contain: revoke the dev's npm/PyPI publish tokens immediately (npm token revoke / pypi web UI), unpublish or deprecate the just-pushed versions if they hit the public registry, force token rotation, quarantine the workstation. 3) Hunt: pivot the SHA256 of any package payload across registry-pull telemetry — any internal team that npm-installed the bad version now needs the same Suspicious Files sweep. Look at every package the token can publish; assume all are compromised until proven clean.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","npm","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "publish")
   or (FileName in~ ("twine.exe","twine") and ProcessCommandLine has "upload")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(npm|pnpm|yarn)\s+publish\b"
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\btwine\s+upload\b"
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("runner.exe","github.runner.worker.exe","gitlab-runner.exe","jenkins.exe","agent.listener.exe","buildkite-agent.exe"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("runner.exe","github.runner.worker.exe","gitlab-runner.exe","jenkins.exe","agent.listener.exe"))
| summarize PublishCount=count(), Cmds=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 25), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where PublishCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "publish")
   or (TargetProcessName has_any ("twine.exe","twine") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "upload")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(npm|pnpm|yarn)\s+publish\b"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\btwine\s+upload\b"
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","gitlab-runner.exe","jenkins.exe","agent.listener.exe","buildkite-agent.exe"))
| summarize PublishCount=count(), Cmds=make_set(TargetProcessCommandLine, 25), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where PublishCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) (@CommandLine:(*"npm publish"* OR *"pnpm publish"* OR *"yarn publish"* OR *"twine upload"*) OR @process.command_line:(*"npm publish"* OR *"twine upload"*)) -@ParentImage:(*\\runner.exe OR *\\Runner.Worker.exe OR *\\jenkins.exe OR *\\gitlab-runner.exe) -@process.executable.path:(/opt/actions-runner/* OR /opt/gitlab-runner/*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("(?i)\\b(npm|pnpm|yarn)\\s+publish\\b|\\btwine\\s+upload\\b", field=CommandLine)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/(runner|Runner\\.Worker|gitlab-runner|jenkins|agent\\.listener|buildkite-agent)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, bin(_time, 10m)], function=count(as=publishCount))
| publishCount >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.dest) as dest from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*npm* publish*" OR Processes.process="*twine* upload*" OR Processes.process="*pnpm* publish*" OR Processes.process="*yarn* publish*") by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines max_match=0 "publish\s+(?<pkg>[A-Za-z0-9@/_.\\-]+)" | eval pkg_count=mvcount(mvdedup(pkg)) | where pkg_count>=3 OR (count>=5)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.dest) as dest from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*npm* publish*" OR Processes.process="*twine* upload*" OR Processes.process="*pnpm* publish*" OR Processes.process="*yarn* publish*") by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines max_match=0 "publish\s+(?<pkg>[A-Za-z0-9@/_.\\-]+)" | eval pkg_count=mvcount(mvdedup(pkg)) | where pkg_count>=3 OR (count>=5)
Hades on-import payload — Bun runtime fetched and executed by Python interpreter AIDelivery High
Detects the Hades PyPI execution chain: a Python interpreter fetches the standalone Bun runtime from the internet and immediately executes it. The article calls this out explicitly — 'the moment a developer imports the package, the hook downloads a standalone Bun runtime and runs a JavaScript payload.' Bun spawned by Python is an extremely strong signal because there is virtually no legitimate Python codebase that drives Bun. Rationale: Article explicitly: 'the hook downloads a standalone Bun runtime and runs a JavaScript payload'. Bun-from-Python is virtually unknown in legitimate workflows — Python projects don't drive Bun. The bun.sh / oven-sh/bun / 'bun-v' URL token pinpoints the runtime download. Cross-checked against: • https://bun.sh • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.007 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Polyglot project where a Python build script legitimately drives a Bun-based frontend build (rare)
  • Developer manually installing Bun via curl|bash piped through a Python wrapper
  • Test/CI environment for cross-runtime tooling where Python invokes Bun deliberately
  • Anaconda/conda-forge package that ships Bun as an optional accelerator (none known today but possible)
  • Security researcher reproducing the Hades chain in a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("build","bundle","vite","esbuild"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which PyPI package's __init__.py kicked off the chain (look at the python invocation cwd, sys.path, or the package directory the parent python was importing). Compare the JS payload Bun ran against the Hades samples publicly reported by StepSecurity. 2) Contain: kill bun.exe, remove the malicious package from site-packages, isolate the workstation if any outbound C2 calls were made, revoke PyPI publishing tokens stored on the host (~/.pypirc, OS keyring), force token+2FA rotation. 3) Hunt: pull every other host in the fleet that imported that same package version (DeviceFileEvents for site-packages/<pkg>/__init__.py with the same SHA256); look for bun.sh DNS/Web requests fleetwide; search for downstream npm/twine publishes from any infected host.
let BunFetch = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-v")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
    | project DownloadTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let BunSpawn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "bun.exe" or FileName =~ "bun"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","node.exe")
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("__init__.py","setup.mjs")
    | project SpawnTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
union BunFetch, BunSpawn
| order by DeviceName asc, coalesce(DownloadTime, SpawnTime) desc
let BunFetch = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any ("bun.sh","oven-sh/bun","bun-v")
    | where SrcUsername != ""
    | project DownloadTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url;
let BunSpawn = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetProcessName has "bun"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3","pythonw.exe","node.exe")
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("__init__.py","setup.mjs")
    | project SpawnTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
union BunFetch, BunSpawn
| order by DvcHostname asc, coalesce(DownloadTime, SpawnTime) desc
title: Python interpreter spawning Bun runtime (Hades PyPI chain)

description: Detects the Hades PyPI worm execution chain where __init__.py downloads and runs a standalone Bun runtime.
references:
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files

    product: windows
detection:
    parent_py:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\python.exe'
            - '\python3.exe'
            - '\pythonw.exe'
    child_bun:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\bun.exe'
            - '\bun'
    condition: parent_py and child_bun
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\pythonw.exe OR *\\Python.exe) @Image:(*\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/python(3|w)?\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\bun(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python3","python")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") OR Processes.process="*bun.sh*" OR Processes.process="*oven-sh/bun*" OR Processes.process="*bun-v*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python3","python")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") OR Processes.process="*bun.sh*" OR Processes.process="*oven-sh/bun*" OR Processes.process="*bun-v*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Miasma Phantom Gyp — 100-300 byte binding.gyp written outside a normal native-addon build AIWeaponization High
Phantom Gyp ships a 157-byte binding.gyp that triggers code execution during npm install's native build step, evading install-script scanners. Detects binding.gyp file writes in the 100-300 byte range outside of legitimate package extraction (tar / git / msiexec parents), then enriches with the immediately-following node-gyp / node.exe child process to confirm code execution. Rationale: Article explicitly: 'Miasma's npm variant uses a technique we call Phantom Gyp: instead of a lifecycle script, it ships a 157-byte binding.gyp file...' The 80-300 byte band brackets that value; legitimate native-addon binding.gyp files are typically 1-5 KB. Cross-checked against: • https://nodejs.org/api/addons.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Lightweight legitimate native-addon packages whose binding.gyp is genuinely small (some toy or minimal C++ addons)
  • Templating tools (yeoman, plop) seeding a placeholder binding.gyp during scaffolding
  • Developer hand-editing a binding.gyp down to a minimal stub while debugging node-gyp build issues
  • Repos vendoring a tiny stub binding.gyp as a marker file with no real native code
  • Test fixtures in node-gyp's own test suite that intentionally ship tiny gyp files
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yo ","plop","scaffold","create-")) and not(FolderPath has "\\node-gyp\\test\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the binding.gyp content. Legitimate ones reference a 'targets' array with C/C++ source files and gyp variables; Phantom Gyp uses gyp's action/condition primitives to shell out to node/curl/sh during the configure or build phase. The file's SHA256 will match across infected packages — pivot it. 2) Contain: block the SHA256 fleetwide, quarantine the workstation, identify the npm package the binding.gyp belongs to (its parent folder under node_modules) and stop any in-flight npm install; revoke npm publish tokens on the host. 3) Hunt: in DeviceProcessEvents look for node.exe / node-gyp / python.exe spawning from npm install within 60s of the binding.gyp write — that's the actual code execution; pivot the package name and SHA256 to every host that npm-installed the same dependency.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where FileSize between (80 .. 300)
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("tar.exe","git.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe","winrar.exe","msiexec.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where TargetFileSize between (80 .. 300)
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("tar.exe","git.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe","winrar.exe","msiexec.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Phantom Gyp — micro binding.gyp dropped
id: 9d8e7f6c-5b4a-3210-9f8e-7d6c5b4a3210
description: Detects creation of a very small binding.gyp file consistent with the Miasma Phantom Gyp 157-byte payload that triggers code execution during npm install's native build step.
references:
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-and-hades-are-spreading-now-detect-them-on-developer-machines-with-suspicious-files
author: StepSecurity research (community port)
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
    - attack.t1195.002
    - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetFilename|endswith: '\binding.gyp'
    condition: selection
level: medium
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @TargetFilename:(*\\binding.gyp OR */binding.gyp)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\\\|/)binding\.gyp$/i
| WrittenBytes < 300
| WrittenBytes >= 80
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(tar|git|7z|7zg|winrar|msiexec|code|devenv)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, WrittenBytes, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="binding.gyp" Filesystem.file_size<300 Filesystem.file_size>=80 by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_size Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(tar|git|msiexec|7z|7zip|winrar)\\.exe$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="binding.gyp" Filesystem.file_size<300 Filesystem.file_size>=80 by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_size Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name, "(?i)(tar|git|msiexec|7z|7zip|winrar)\\.exe$")
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Gentlemen BYOVD driver file dropped to disk (eb.sys, nseckrnl.sys, ThrottleBlood.sys, havoc.sys, etc.) · [LLM] GentleKiller dropper executable in staging directory or AV-impersonating filename · [LLM] Kernel-mode service registration for Gentlemen BYOVD drivers (Havoc service / %TEMP%\*.sys ImagePath)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mass termination of EDR/AV processes by single non-system process (GentleKiller behavioral) · [LLM] OxideHarvest credential stealer command-line pattern (-i hosts -u user -p pass -o output) · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Gentlemen BYOVD driver file dropped to disk (eb.sys, nseckrnl.sys, ThrottleBlood.sys, havoc.sys, etc.) AIInstallation High
Detects file writes of the specific .sys driver filenames associated with the GentleKiller / HexKiller / ThrottleBlood / HavocKiller variants documented by ESET. Each variant drops a named vulnerable or malicious driver before loading it, so the on-disk artifact is the earliest high-fidelity pivot. Rationale: Driver filenames eb.sys, nseckrnl.sys, ThrottleBlood.sys, havoc.sys, dmx.sys, etc. are explicitly named by ESET as artifacts of GentleKiller / HexKiller / ThrottleBlood / HavocKiller variants and corroborated by BleepingComputer + Huntress. Cross-checked against the SHA-1 list in the article. Excluded vgk.sys + GameDriverX64.sys to avoid Valorant/Vanguard FPs — those collide with legitimate gaming. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/gentlemen-ransomware-uses-multiple-edr-killers-to-disable-defenses/ • https://www.huntress.com/blog/w2-malvertising-to-kernel-mode-edr-kill • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/18/eset-gentlemen-edr-killers/
ATT&CKT1068 T1014 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Safetica DLP installation creates stpm_old.sys / stpm_new.sys to its install path
  • Zemana Antimalware install drops dmx.sys
  • Qihoo 360 Total Security install drops 360netmon_wfp.sys
  • Forensic tool unzipping a sample collection containing one of these driver names
  • Security researcher loading a sample for analysis in a sandbox VM
Suppression filter
| where not(FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Program Files(?: \(x86\))?\\(Safetica|Zemana|Qihoo 360|Baidu|Huawei|TechPowerUp|NSecsoft)\\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("GentlemenCollection","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the dropped .sys against the article's SHA-1 list; check ESET signature name on InitiatingProcessFileName. Pull DeviceProcessEvents for the dropper that created the file, look for matching Kasps.exe / FaceIT*.exe / EASolo*.exe / Deletor.exe naming. 2) Contain: isolate the host (MDE Isolate), kill the dropping process tree, block SHA256 of the .sys at the EDR layer, query all hosts for the same file. 3) Hunt: search the last 30d for the same driver across the org, pivot on the dropper's parent (often a ransomware loader or RDP session), look for ShadowCopy deletion and lsass dumps following the driver load — these precede encryption.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName in~ ("eb.sys","nseckrnl.sys","stpm_old.sys","stpm_new.sys","dmx.sys","360netmon_wfp.sys","G11.sys","googleApiUtil64.sys","ThrottleBlood.sys","havoc.sys","IMFForceDelete.sys")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
// Exclude legitimate vendor installer paths — Gentlemen drops to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, %PUBLIC%, or staging dir
| where not(FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Program Files(?: \(x86\))?\\(Safetica|Zemana|Qihoo 360|Baidu|Huawei|TechPowerUp|NSecsoft)\\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("eb.sys","nseckrnl.sys","stpm_old.sys","stpm_new.sys","dmx.sys","360netmon_wfp.sys","G11.sys","googleApiUtil64.sys","ThrottleBlood.sys","havoc.sys","IMFForceDelete.sys")
| where not(TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Program Files(?: \(x86\))?\\(Safetica|Zemana|Qihoo 360|Baidu|Huawei|TechPowerUp|NSecsoft)\\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername,
          TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Gentlemen Ransomware BYOVD Driver File Drop

status: experimental

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\eb.sys OR *\\EB.SYS OR *\\nseckrnl.sys OR *\\NSECKRNL.SYS OR *\\stpm_old.sys OR *\\stpm_new.sys OR *\\dmx.sys OR *\\DMX.SYS OR *\\360netmon_wfp.sys OR *\\G11.sys OR *\\googleApiUtil64.sys OR *\\ThrottleBlood.sys OR *\\throttleblood.sys OR *\\havoc.sys OR *\\Havoc.sys OR *\\HAVOC.SYS OR *\\IMFForceDelete.sys)) NOT @TargetFilename:(*\\Program?Files\\Safetica\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\Zemana\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\TechPowerUp\\*)
